weekendGames.title: Budget Battle
weekendGames.description: Can you make smart choices with a limited monthly income?
weekendGames.learningGoal: Understand budgeting, saving, and the trade-offs behind everyday spending.

scenario.intro: You earn ₹30,000 this month. Your essential expenses are covered, but you have ₹10,000 left for flexible spending and saving.

rounds.question: You have ₹10,000 left. What do you do first?

options.text: Save ₹4,000 and keep ₹6,000 for flexible spending
options.feedback: Good balance. You are setting money aside before spending everything.

options.text: Spend the full ₹10,000 because the essentials are already paid
options.feedback: You can spend it, but leaving nothing for savings or unexpected needs reduces your financial buffer.

options.text: Invest the entire ₹10,000 immediately
options.feedback: Investing can be useful, but your short-term needs and emergency savings should also be considered.

rounds.question: A friend invites you to a ₹2,500 dinner. Your flexible spending budget is getting tight.

options.text: Go, but reduce another non-essential expense this month
options.feedback: A planned trade-off helps you enjoy the expense without losing control of your budget.

options.text: Go and use credit without checking your budget
options.feedback: Credit can make spending feel easier, but the expense still has to be paid later.

options.text: Never spend money on anything fun
options.feedback: A budget does not mean avoiding all enjoyment. The goal is to spend intentionally.

rounds.question: You have ₹3,000 remaining near the end of the month.

options.text: Keep most of it as savings and carry some forward
options.feedback: Unused money can strengthen your savings and give you more flexibility next month.

options.text: Spend it all because the month is almost over
options.feedback: A month ending does not mean unused money must be spent.

options.text: Lend all of it to a friend without considering your own needs
options.feedback: Helping others is a personal choice, but your own financial needs should also be considered.

messages.title: Strong Budgeter
messages.message: You made choices that balanced spending, saving, and flexibility.

messages.title: Getting There
messages.message: You understand some budgeting basics, but a little more planning could help.

messages.title: Budget Practice Needed
messages.message: Small spending decisions can add up. Try planning your priorities before spending.

weekendGames.title: Scam Detective
weekendGames.description: Spot the warning signs before a suspicious message catches you off guard.
weekendGames.learningGoal: Recognize common financial scam signals and safer responses.

rounds.question: You receive: 'Your bank account will be blocked today. Click this link immediately to update your KYC.' What should you do?

options.text: Click the link and update KYC quickly
options.feedback: Urgency plus an unknown link is a major warning sign. Do not click it.

options.text: Ignore the link and contact the bank through its official channel
options.feedback: Correct. Verify account issues directly through the bank's official app, website, or phone number.

options.text: Forward the message to friends to ask what they think
options.feedback: Sharing suspicious links can expose others to the same scam. Verify through an official source instead.

rounds.question: Someone calls claiming to be from your bank and asks for your OTP to 'reverse a failed transaction.'

options.text: Give the OTP because they know your recent transaction
options.feedback: Never share an OTP. A caller knowing transaction details does not prove they are genuine.

options.text: Refuse and contact your bank using the official number
options.feedback: Correct. Keep OTPs, PINs, passwords, and other authentication details private.

options.text: Give only the last two digits of the OTP
options.feedback: Partial OTP information can still be useful to scammers. Do not share it.

rounds.question: An online post promises 'guaranteed 5x returns in 30 days' with no risk.

options.text: Invest immediately before the offer disappears
options.feedback: Guaranteed high returns with no risk are a major red flag.

options.text: Research the offer and verify the entity through reliable official sources
options.feedback: Correct. Verify before sending money or sharing financial information.

options.text: Invest a small amount just to test it
options.feedback: Even a small payment can expose you to fraud. Verify first.

messages.title: Scam Spotter
messages.message: You consistently noticed urgency, secrecy, suspicious links, and unrealistic promises.

messages.title: Stay Alert
messages.message: You caught some warning signs. Keep practicing safe verification habits.

messages.title: Scam Signals Missed
messages.message: Pause before clicking, paying, or sharing sensitive information. Verification is your first defence.

weekendGames.title: Needs vs Wants
weekendGames.description: You have limited money. Can you prioritize what matters most?
weekendGames.learningGoal: Distinguish essential expenses from optional spending and prioritize financial needs.

rounds.question: You have ₹5,000 available after paying your main bills. Your phone is working fine, but a new model costs ₹4,500.

options.text: Buy the new phone because it is on sale
options.feedback: A discount does not automatically make something necessary.

options.text: Keep the money for savings or upcoming needs
options.feedback: Good choice. A working phone means the upgrade is optional, not essential.

options.text: Borrow money to buy the phone
options.feedback: Borrowing for an unnecessary purchase can create an avoidable financial burden.

rounds.question: Your monthly transport cost is increasing. You can either pay for essential travel or spend the same amount on entertainment.

options.text: Prioritize the transport expense
options.feedback: Essential expenses should generally come before discretionary spending.

options.text: Spend on entertainment and figure out transport later
options.feedback: Delaying an essential expense can create bigger problems later.

options.text: Split the money equally without checking your actual needs
options.feedback: Splitting money can work sometimes, but priorities should be based on actual needs and deadlines.

rounds.question: You want a ₹2,000 pair of shoes, but your current shoes are usable and you have an upcoming college fee.

options.text: Pay the college fee first and delay the shoes
options.feedback: You prioritized a known financial obligation over an optional purchase.

options.text: Buy the shoes and worry about the fee later
options.feedback: An optional purchase should not normally take priority over an upcoming essential payment.

options.text: Use credit for the shoes
options.feedback: Credit does not remove the cost. It can make an optional purchase more expensive if interest or fees apply.

messages.title: Priority Pro
messages.message: You consistently separated essential needs from optional wants.

messages.title: Think Before You Spend
messages.message: You made some good priorities, but a pause before optional purchases can help.

messages.title: Needs First
messages.message: Start by identifying what must be paid before deciding what you can afford to spend.

weekendGames.title: Money Decision Tree
weekendGames.description: A surprise expense forces you to make a financial decision. What will you do?
weekendGames.learningGoal: Understand how financial decisions change based on urgency, available savings, and borrowing costs.

rounds.question: An unexpected ₹8,000 expense comes up. You have ₹20,000 in emergency savings.

options.text: Use part of your emergency savings and review your budget
options.feedback: This is one purpose of an emergency fund: handling unexpected necessary expenses.

options.text: Borrow immediately even though you have enough savings
options.feedback: Borrowing may add interest or fees when you already have funds available.

options.text: Ignore the expense completely
options.feedback: Ignoring a necessary expense can make the problem more costly.

rounds.question: Your savings can cover the expense, but using them would reduce your emergency fund significantly.

options.text: Use only what is necessary and make a plan to rebuild the fund
options.feedback: Good approach. Use the fund for the need, then work toward restoring it.

options.text: Spend extra money because you have already touched your savings
options.feedback: Using savings for one need does not make additional spending free.

options.text: Take a high-cost loan without comparing alternatives
options.feedback: Borrowing costs matter. Compare options and understand the total repayment before borrowing.

rounds.question: After the emergency, you receive ₹5,000 of extra income. What is a sensible next step?

options.text: Put a large part toward rebuilding your emergency savings
options.feedback: Rebuilding your financial buffer can improve your ability to handle the next unexpected expense.

options.text: Spend all ₹5,000 because you had a difficult month
options.feedback: Enjoyment is fine, but using all extra income may leave your emergency fund weaker.

options.text: Put all ₹5,000 into a random investment without researching it
options.feedback: Financial products should be understood before money is committed. Your immediate safety net may also need attention.

messages.title: Calm Decision Maker
messages.message: You considered urgency, savings, and future financial resilience before acting.

messages.title: Good Instincts
messages.message: You showed some strong habits. Comparing costs and planning ahead can make decisions stronger.

messages.title: Pause and Plan
messages.message: Before borrowing or spending, check urgency, available savings, total costs, and future needs.
